steps.title: Create the two-scene transition fixture
preconditions: Run the document-integrity service through the actual Scriv CLI, after its earlier graph, boundary and timeline chapters, against the bundled production Worker in an owned local Miniflare process.
Synthetic users, sessions and a paid team are preseeded only for access; no login, team administration, live account, billing, provider or native UI behavior is under test.

This continuation creates its own project by public HTTP. All requests use the existing bounded loopback request helper, denied outbound network and owned process cleanup. Item leases are acquired publicly and remain valid during this bounded chapter; expiry and concurrency are outside scope.

Expected full document items, versions, sequence, timing, receipts and history are authored from fixture inputs. Snapshot comparison omits expiring leases; it does not establish internal table contents, crash durability, transient behavior, image bytes or measured source execution.

expectations.description: Project creation returns 201. The empty public state is exact. The seven-item graph saves with all item versions one, sequence one, timing one and one exact event, with source and destination cues each covering [0,1000] in their own scenes.

expectations.description: Missing and wrong-kind predecessor references and image character tags reject with 400 invalid_reference; self, equal and decreasing revisions reject with 400 image_version. A valid version-two revision followed by its version-one predecessor in the same command succeeds with exact saved items and references, sequence three, unchanged timing two and one exact event. Both image item versions are one, distinct from their data.version values; all rejected attempts preserve the full public snapshot excluding leases and event stream.

mappings.why: Public image character-tag and predecessor references reject absent/wrong-kind targets and accept the correct character plus complete same-command image predecessor.
A self-reference and equal/decreasing revision numbers reject, while a strictly increasing revision with a separately identified predecessor persists exactly.
